cells.tense: You are setting a structure down, and what each person puts in comes back around.
cells.act: set the finished thing down in a form that keeps
cells.ask: Write the arrangement you have working into a couple of plain lines anyone could follow, then leave it through an evening where nothing needs deciding.
cells.core:
You're making structure here, and the give-and-take inside it is honest — people put in, people get back, and it doesn't last only as long as your attention does. That's why it holds past the room it was made in; the pattern is sound, not merely watched.

The work that's left can't be done by defining anything. Take one piece of the exchange you've set up, keep it exactly as it is this week, and don't improve it. A fair pattern needs a stretch where no one touches it and it stays standing. That's the whole test, and it asks very little of you.
cells.sheetLine: The fairness is real, and it can stand without your hand.
cells.place: where structure is set and a pattern is being made to hold

cells.tense: You will be checking who gave what before the pattern has even finished setting.
cells.act: carry your own share, all of it
cells.ask: For a week, carry your own part of this fully and let others carry theirs. When the tally starts, look at what has been built instead.
cells.core:
The pattern here keeps turning, and a tally runs alongside it — who gave what, who came up short. While the form is still being laid down, the counting starts before it can settle. The fairness isn't wrong; it has got out past the structure it belongs to, and the people on the other end can tell they're being weighed.

Watch for the moment you start checking before anyone has actually fallen short, and put the check down. For a week, keep your own share fully and leave the pattern unfinished if that's what it is. Much of what looks owed settles by itself before the week is done. One look then, if you still want one.
cells.sheetLine: The accounting is outrunning the pattern.
cells.place: where structure is set and a pattern is being made to hold

cells.tense: You set the structure down and stopped putting your own share into the exchange.
cells.act: sort what matters from what does not, carefully
cells.ask: Take a week of what you put into this and mark which parts hold it up and which go nowhere. Cross one item off the second list.
cells.core:
You build order here — containers, the form other people move inside — and in the give-and-take of it you put in and take nothing out. The pattern gets its hours and the return doesn't land. Things come toward you and slide by.

Look at what you actually put in, not at what you feel about it. Sort one plain week: what held the structure up, and what went in without coming back. Cross out a single item from the second list, and let that time go empty — no pattern in it, nothing held — so a little of it returns to you and you can feel that it did.
cells.sheetLine: You give to what you build and take nothing back.

cells.tense: The hand that keeps the pattern fair is already at work, and it does not come to mind as yours.
cells.act: pause before you let it be known
cells.ask: The next time the exchange tips and you move to even it, wait a beat. In that beat, know this is you doing it.
cells.core:
There's a hand keeping things fair among the people near you — evening a margin here, easing off there so someone else comes out level — and a real structure has come out of it. Ask the hand's owner and they'll say things just sort themselves out among you. They don't. You do.

Next time the balance tips, hold for a second before you set it right. Nothing else changes: you can still move, or not. But that second is where the one keeping things fair and the one merely present stop being the same person. That's the whole difference, and nobody needs to hear it said.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the exchange fair. What you call it is things working out.
cells.place: where structure is set and a pattern is being made to hold
